key_insight: A synchronized multi-camera platform enables reliable, real-time 3D tracking and coordination for simultaneous human–robot interactions in cluttered, close‑proximity home environments, overcoming persistent occlusion and rapid state changes.
problem_solved: Addresses the bottleneck of unreliable real-time 3D state estimation in multiadic home settings—where multiple humans and robots act concurrently with tight spatial and temporal coupling and frequent occlusions.
method: Synchronized multi-camera hardware and coverage design to reduce persistent occlusions in close‑quarters domestic scenes.
Low-latency sensor fusion and occlusion‑aware multi-agent 3D tracking pipeline that maintains consistent identities and states under rapid interactions.
Integration of tracked states with robot control and coordination modules to support concurrent, interleaved subtasks among multiple humans and robots.
impact: Makes multiadic human–robot collaboration practical in real homes by providing the sensing and tracking foundation needed for safe, coordinated multi-agent behaviors. Enables researchers and practitioners to develop, benchmark, and deploy concurrent multi-person multi-robot applications.
visual_elements: Floorplan illustration of a home environment showing multiple cameras, humans, and robots with coverage cones and tracked 3D trajectories.
Pipeline diagram of synchronized cameras → sensor fusion → occlusion‑aware multi-agent tracker → robot controller.
Before/after occlusion comparison: single camera failing vs. multi-camera tracking maintaining consistent identities through occlusion.
Latency and robustness chart (e.g., tracking accuracy vs. occlusion level and end-to-end latency) to highlight real‑time performance.
paper_title: OmniRobotHome: A Multi-Camera Platform for Real-Time Multiadic Human-Robot Interaction
paper_authors: Junyoung Lee, Sookwan Han, Jeonghwan Kim, Inhee Lee, Mingi Choi
